idea-plugin.name: Trace Tail
idea-plugin.description:
Live view of the logs of the Java applications you run from the IDE, grouped by the request they belong to.

Each request is a single row; selecting it shows its log lines beside it, nested by trace.id, span.id and parent.id. So for a request that passes through several applications, you can see at a glance which steps it took, which step started which, and where it failed.

  • Tree: one row per request, with its line count, outcome, duration and the number of WARN and ERROR lines; selecting it shows its steps beside it
  • Sequence: the selected request as a diagram of who called whom across apps, classes, queues and outside systems; Copy as Mermaid copies it as text
  • Flat: every line in arrival order, coloured per request; clicking a request's id fades the others out, and stack trace frames link to the source
  • Raw: the JSON lines as the agent sent them
  • A Trace Tail tab in each Run and Debug window, showing only the requests that run took part in
  • Jump to Source (F4) from a log line to the class that wrote it
  • A level filter per app, pause, Scroll to the End and Soft-Wrap

The application needs no added dependency and no change to its logging configuration. When a Java run configuration is run or debugged, the plugin adds its agent to the JVM. The agent adds an appender to the application's Logback (1.2 or later) or Log4j2 (2.17 or later), which sends each log event as an ECS JSON line to the IDE over a loopback port. The application runs on Java 8 or later.

See the README for the fields the view reads.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.5.4

  • Open in Window in the Sequence tab's toolbar opens the diagram in a window of its own, which keeps showing the same requests while others are selected
  • The Sequence diagram draws an HZ_EMBEDDED call to its own Hazelcast lifeline inside the app's box instead of back to the app; an HZ_OUT call still goes to the Hazelcast outside it
  • The Sequence diagram labels a DB_OUT call with its target and operation, such as OrderRepository.findById

1.5.3

  • The Sequence diagram draws a LIFECYCLE step on a lifeline for its target class, kept next to its app, and labels it with its operation

1.5.2

  • The selected line's JSON beside the steps starts closed; Show Line JSON in the toolbar opens and closes it
  • The Sequence diagram draws a DB_OUT call to a database lifeline, labelled with its operation

1.5.1

  • The Sequence diagram draws an HZ_OUT call to a Hazelcast lifeline and keeps an HZ_EMBEDDED call on the app's own lifeline; both are labelled with the map and the operation

1.5.0

  • The Tree lists each request as one row; selecting it opens its steps in a new Steps tab beside it. The selected line's JSON and stack trace, which had a Line tab, show on the steps' right
  • The IDE remembers where the Tree's dividers were dragged, and the Run windows' Trace Tail tabs open the same way
  • Only the selected requests are laid out line by line: a request no longer lays out all its lines again each time one arrives, so long requests no longer slow the Tree down
  • Expand All and Collapse All act on Steps; Collapse All keeps each request open on its first steps

1.4.1

  • Replaces the deprecated and internal IntelliJ API that IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 warns about

1.4.0

  • Each run keeps as much text as its console would (Settings | Editor | General | Console); past that, its oldest request goes, from every app and all three tabs. A request that got a line in the last 30 seconds loses only its oldest lines, but never its START alone
  • All runs together keep at most 50,000 lines; past that, the run with the most lines loses its oldest request
  • A changed level filter no longer shrinks the Tree
  • Rerun, closing a Run or Debug tab and Clear All in a run's console delete that run's lines; the other runs' lines of the same requests stay
  • The agent sends the process id; the Run window's Trace Tail tab shows the requests of its run, so two runs of one configuration are told apart
  • Flat and Raw are editors: lines can go from anywhere while the lines being read stay in place
  • Each tab's status line counts what it shows; the port, the apps and the limit are in its tooltip

1.3.0

  • Sequence draws LDAP_OUT calls to an ldap lifeline and MAIL_OUT calls to a mail lifeline, each labelled with its op
  • WS_IN frames come from the user and WS_OUT frames go to them, labelled with the STOMP command and destination
  • An HTTP_OUT call is drawn at the app that took it, whatever the caller named its target

1.2.0

  • Shift and Ctrl select several rows in the Tree; Line and Sequence show them one under the other
  • Ctrl+C in the Tree copies the request ids of the selected rows
  • Show in Flat, in the Tree's context menu, opens the Flat tab on the line with its request focused
  • Scroll to the End turns on as soon as the Tree is scrolled up
  • END rows line up with their START in the Tree

1.1.2: a new plugin logo.

1.1.1: updated screenshots; the plugin no longer uses internal or experimental platform API.

1.1.0

  • A plugin logo
  • Each request keeps at most 5,000 lines
  • The Tree keeps its selection while requests come in
  • The START tag shows only on an open row
  • The status line shows the Tree's line count

1.0.0: the first release.

  • Tree, Flat and Raw tabs, with the selected line (Line) and request (Sequence) beside the Tree
  • Sequence diagrams of a request across apps, which can be copied as Mermaid
  • A Trace Tail tab in each Run and Debug window
  • Logs sent by a Java agent from Logback 1.2 or later and Log4j2 2.17 or later, with no change to the application
  • Level filter, pause, Scroll to the End, Soft-Wrap and Jump to Source
